AUTHOR: Jansen
TITLE: Monitoring tropical freshwater fish with underwater videography and deep learning
REGION: Alligator Rivers Region / Kakadu National Park, Northern Territory, Australia (Mudginberri, Sandy, Gulungul, Georgetown billabongs)
SPECIES: 23 tropical freshwater taxa: Ambassis macleayi, A. agrammus, Amniataba percoides, Craterocephalus stercusmuscarum, Melanotaenia splendida inornata, Neosilurus spp., Lates calcarifer, Toxotes chatareus, etc. (genus level for Neosilurus, Glossogobius, Oxyeleotris, Neoarius)
DATA: Own footage: 392 unbaited GoPro deployments 2016–2019 (channel billabongs) + 180 deployments 2019 (backflow billabongs) → 44,112 annotated images / 82,904 boxes; independent test set of 286 one-hour videos (2020–2022)
V_EV: Training dataset criteria: 'Deteriorating light and turbidity also make identification difficult. Annotations were only made in clear conditions satisfying these criteria.' No turbidity measurement; poor-visibility frames excluded without characterisation.
D2: Training imagery 2016–2019 (Azure internal 80:20 image split for training metrics); independent test set = 286 videos from May 2020, 2021, 2022
D_EV: Test dataset: 'An independent test dataset was derived from two-hundred eighty-six 1-h video files collected from channel billabong fish monitoring (Mudginberri and Sandy) in May 2020, 2021 and 2022'
R_EV: Discussion: 'This difference in accuracy between the model's training metrics (e.g. 83.6% mAP) and its performance in real-world situations (e.g. 54.4% MaxN-F1)'
C_EV: Methods: 'Optimum thresholds per taxon were selected from the highest MaxN-F1 score achieved.'; Results: 'Thresholds ranged between 70 and 99.9%'
E_EV: Abstract/Methods: 'Fish abundance (MaxN) was measured by trained observers and deep learning'; Results: 'PERMANOVA results showed significant differences between methods ... billabongs ... and among the years'; 'reflect the same relative changes between Mudginberri and Sandy billabongs over a 3-year period'.
ARCH: Microsoft Azure Custom Vision object detection (general domain model, 96 h training; compact edge model also trained) — architecture not user-selectable/undisclosed
METR: Precision, recall, mAP per taxon (Azure 20% test); MaxN-precision, MaxN-recall, MaxN-F1 per taxon vs observers (n=286 videos); Bray–Curtis / PCO / three-way PERMANOVA
NOTE: Two evaluation layers: (1) Azure-internal 80:20 split parsed from the annotated images (unit not stated, presumably image-level) giving mAP 83.6%; (2) independent test set of 286 one-hour videos from 2020–2022 at the same two billabongs, used for MaxN comparison with trained observers. D1=조사일 and D_ALL=Y are coded on layer (2) (temporal separation by survey year); a verifier who treats only the Azure split as 'the' split would get D1=이미지/프레임 무작위 → D_ALL=N. D4=Y because the paper explicitly contrasts training-split metrics with independent real-world performance. R1=Y/R2=계절/시기 reflects later survey years at the same sites (same cameras/habitat) — borderline external; no other site/dataset. C5=없음 chosen conservatively: FP counts are reported at the MaxN-per-video level against observer MaxN (e.g. '143 FP predictions at 95% threshold compared to 3 FP predictions at 99.9%'), not as human verification of a detection sample; if accepted as C5=검증 표본 오탐률, C_ALL would become Y. V_ALL=N (frames annotated only in clear conditions, no quantification) although V1=정성 서술만 would otherwise give P. FPS=Y refers to frame extraction at 1 frame per second, not native camera frame rate. MaxN-recall per taxon is reported but not framed as FNR (E4=없음). Training data on Zenodo (record 7250921), code on GitHub (ajansenn/KakaduFishAI); the general Azure model itself is not publicly available.
